newsitem.title: USA: Muni yield curve flattens slightly over past week.
newsitem.headline: Muni yield curve flattens slightly over past week.

text.p: The municipal yield curve flattened slightly over the week ended Thursday, as one-year maturities gained five basis points and the rest of the market held steady, Delphis Hanover Corp said on Friday.
Treasuries outperformed munis for the week. The government long bond dropped nine basis points to finish Thursday at a 6.80 percent yield.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated municipal yields, in contrast, were unchanged for the second week in a row at 5.60 percent. Thirty-year Baa yields were also steady at 6.40 percent.
In the intermediate sector, ten-year Aaa-rated and Baa-rated muni yields were both unchanged for the second consecutive week, holding at 4.95 percent and 5.75 percent, respectively.
Average yields on one-year Aaa-rated municipal bonds rose five basis points across the credit spectrum, moving to 3.75 percent for Aaa-rated bonds and 4.55 percent for Baa's.
The Aaa municipal yield curve flattened five basis points to 185, while the spread between one-year and 30-year Baa's reversed the prior week's widening, flattening five to 185 basis points.
The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years was unchanged for the third consecutive week at 80 basis points. The 30-year spread was also unchanged at 80 basis points.
